Prism

Your API, tested as flows.

Chain requests so each one hands its values to the next, check every response, and run the whole flow on your desktop or in CI. Imports Postman, OpenAPI, HAR and cURL. Free for Windows.

Flows

Chain it once.

When one request captures a value — a token, an order id — and another uses it, Prism draws the connection and runs them in that order. No wiring step: the flow is the test, and Run flow reports every stop on a departure board.

  • Captures from the body or a header
  • Auth set once on a collection or flow
  • Conditions, waits, loops and polling
  • Pre-request and test scripts with Postman’s pm
Prism

Checks

Check what came back.

Eleven kinds of check and over forty ways to compare — status, time, headers, JSON paths with wildcards, formats, JSON Schema, cookies. Each one says what it saw, beside the response it saw it in.

Prism

Generate

Tests read off a real response.

Generate proposes checks from the last response — types, formats and shape rather than today’s values — and runs each one against it before offering it. Or pick from a library of 55.

Prism

Export

Code that keeps its checks.

Export to 15 targets — cURL, Python, pytest, fetch, axios, Playwright, Java, REST Assured, C#, Go, PHP, Postman and OpenAPI — with every check written out. A token never lands in a file: it comes out as an environment variable.

Prism

Run timeline

What changed since the last run?

Every run of a flow is kept. Pick any two and Prism says what broke, what was fixed, what got slower and which fields appeared, vanished or changed type.

Prism

Load test

How much can it take?

Send a flow with up to 50 users at once, with a ramp-up and think time. Watch requests per second, p50, p95 and errors as it runs — and set a budget it either keeps or doesn’t.

Prism

Mock server

An API before the API.

Prism answers in your API’s place at 127.0.0.1 — from frozen baselines, the last responses and your OpenAPI examples — so a front end can work while the back end isn’t ready. Only your computer can reach it.

Prism

Console

See exactly what went out.

Every request as it was sent and as it came back — headers, bodies, status and time — with script logs and errors beside it. Credentials stay masked until you ask.

Prism

CI

Run it headless.

Started with --cli, Prism runs the same workspace file on your runner — with data files, iterations and an HTML, JUnit or JSON report — and exits 1 when a check fails.

Which one do you need?

Three tools, three jobs. All free, all on your own computer.

  • Driftly

    Know if a release is safe to ship.

    Watches your live sites — visual changes, security, speed and APIs — and gives one GO or NO-GO before each release. Its recorder replays a few key flows inside those checks.

    Meet Driftly

  • Tracemend

    Build the test suite you keep.

    Turns flows you record into Playwright, Selenium, Cypress or WebdriverIO code your team owns — with page objects, accessibility checks, phones and tablets, and a CLI for CI — and keeps it healing as the site changes.

    Meet Tracemend

  • PrismYou’re here

    Test your API, flow by flow.

    A workspace for API testing: requests chained into flows, checks on every response, load tests, a mock server and code in 15 formats — with a command-line runner for CI.

Tech specs

Version

Latest

0.1.0

Released

20 Oct 2026

Platform

Operating system

Windows 10 or Windows 11, 64-bit (x64)

Disk space

About 325 MB installed

macOS and Linux

Coming soon

Installer

Type

Windows installer, for you only — no administrator rights needed; you choose the folder

Download size

Published with each download

Verification

SHA-256 checksum published for every file

Updates

No automatic updates or update checks — new versions are published here

Code signing

Not code-signed yet — Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run. Verify the published SHA-256 first.

Code-signed Windows installers, with a published SHA-256 for every file.

Licence

Free · closed source

Free for personal and commercial use, under the Prism EULA. The workspaces, reports and code you make with it are yours.

Your data

Location

Your workspace files, wherever you save them; settings and backups in %APPDATA%\Prism

Privacy

No accounts, analytics, telemetry or update checks — the only traffic is the requests you send

Secrets

A secret’s value is never written to a workspace, a backup or an export; in CI it comes from PRISM_<NAME>

For Git

One .prism.json file, or a folder with a file per request

Requests

Protocols

  • GraphQL
  • WebSocket
  • Server-Sent Events

Auth

  • Bearer
  • Basic
  • API key

  • JWT
  • Inherited from the collection or flow

Scripts

Pre-request and test scripts in JavaScript with Postman’s pm object — sandboxed, with no network, stopped after 5 seconds

Logic

  • Run only if
  • Wait
  • Repeat for each
  • Repeat until
  • Stop the flow

How to verify your download

Compute the SHA-256 of the file

Get-FileHash "$HOME\Downloads\Prism Setup 0.1.0.exe" -Algorithm SHA256

Compute the SHA-256 of the file

shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/"Prism Setup 0.1.0.exe"

Compute the SHA-256 of the file

shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/"Prism Setup 0.1.0.exe"
# or: sha256sum ~/Downloads/"Prism Setup 0.1.0.exe"

Compare the result with the SHA-256 published next to the file. If they differ, delete the file and download it again.

What’s new in 0.1.0

v0.1.020 Oct 2026
  • First public release, for Windows 10 and 11 (x64).
  • Requests chained into flows on a map, with captures, inherited auth, conditions, loops and polling.
  • Eleven kinds of check, generated tests and a library of 55; OpenAPI contract checks on every response.
  • HTTP, GraphQL, WebSocket, Server-Sent Events and gRPC.
  • The Runner with data files and HTML, JUnit and JSON reports; load tests, schedules, a mock server and a run timeline.
  • Imports Postman, OpenAPI, HAR and cURL; exports to 15 targets with every check written out.
  • A command-line runner for CI: Prism.exe --cli.
